question: What filesystem boundary should OpenClaw expose for host-mode agents: a `tools.fs` allow/deny PathGuard policy, a `tools.fs.roots` access-mode policy, or a narrower workspace-only plus separate exec-deny design?
rationale: This defines a public config surface and security boundary, and the active implementation candidates make different compatibility, migration, and false-security tradeoffs that automation should not choose.

options.title: Choose one `tools.fs` path-policy contract
options.body: Settle the canonical config shape, require normalization/symlink/deny-precedence tests, and make exec coverage explicit before merging either implementation path.

options.title: Split exec into a separate security tracker
options.body: Allow a file-tool-only policy only if docs and labels clearly state that shell-mediated file access remains a separate boundary.

options.title: Defer to OS or container isolation
options.body: Reject or downgrade the host filesystem ACL request if maintainers decide OpenClaw should not own path-level host ACLs beyond workspaceOnly and sandbox backends.

recommendation.title: Choose one `tools.fs` path-policy contract
recommendation.body: Settle the canonical config shape, require normalization/symlink/deny-precedence tests, and make exec coverage explicit before merging either implementation path.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already framed the prior keep-open review and has the strongest current history on the workspaceOnly config/schema/security path.
